| [QUESTION-049](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-049.md) | When a corporation is said to know or intend something no member does, is the attribution tracking a mind the corporation has, or shaping the corporation to meet it? | An unmarked tension between two THEORYs the record holds, raised by the synthesis review of 2026-10-11. | [QUESTION-053](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-053.md) | Does organizational affect need a group subject, a state of the group not reducible to its members' states, or only the synchronized convergence of members' affect? | An unmarked tension between two THEORYs the record holds, raised by the synthesis review of 2026-10-11. [THEORY-125](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-125.md) (Huebner) allows a group to be in an emotional state that is not its members' states in aggregation. [THEORY-126](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-126.md) (von Scheve and Ismer) makes collective emotion synchronous convergence with no group subject. | [QUESTION-073](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-073.md) | Are teasing and reproach individuated by the speaker's communicative intention, or partly by a frame the parties sustain together and by their standing? | Raised by [CLAIM-221](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-221.md) and [CLAIM-224](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-224.md) on 2026-10-10. Intention-based accounts of illocution (Grice; Strawson 1964; Bach and Harnish 1979) plausibly individuate teasing by the speaker's intention. Goffman's account of keying a play frame and Austin's securing of uptake ([LIT-785](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-785.md), unread) are the tradition's replies. None of these is read here. An answer would read them and find a case in which the speaker's intention is held fixed and the act verdicts of informed participants change with the parties' standing or uptake. | Open |
